_meta.units: thickness_pct and camber_pct in % chord; angles in deg; Cm about the quarter chord
_meta.method: XFOIL polars from airfoiltools.com (Ncrit 9, Mach 0), NOT wind-tunnel data. Values derived from the polar CSV that was downloaded (the 'source_polar_*' URL): clmax = largest Cl in the polar; alpha_0 and cm0 = linear interpolation at Cl = 0; cl_alpha_per_deg = least-squares slope over alpha -2..4 deg; cm_range = min..max Cm over alpha -2..6 deg (the normal flight range). XFOIL tends to over-predict 2D CLmax by ~0.05-0.15 at these Re; a 3D swept wing reaches ~0.8-0.9 of the 2D value (see projects/fpv_wing/REFERENCES.md).
_meta.thickness_method: max thickness from the .dat resampled on 2001 chord stations (numpy.interp of upper and lower surfaces)

MH45.note: XFOIL, Ncrit 9. Designer: MH 40/60 series aim at 'small torsion (cm c/4) coefficients' and higher CLmax than older low-cm sections; the MH 44/45/46/49 group 'seem to work quite well, even at Reynolds numbers below 200000'. airfoiltools lists max thickness 9.8 % at 26.9 %, camber 1.7 % at 36.6 %. At a 1 m wing's 70 km/h cruise the root (~250 mm) runs Re ~330k and the tip (~170 mm) ~220k, so the 200k figures are the conservative design values.

MH60.note: XFOIL, Ncrit 9. airfoiltools: 10.1 % at 26.9 %, camber 1.7 % at 36.6 %, 'designed for flying wings'. Slightly thicker than MH 45 (more spar depth), very slightly more nose-down Cm and lower CLmax at Re 200k; an alternative root section, not needed at this size.
